title: Three walks stop on a panel control the dock has scrolled out of reach
goal: Three scripted walks stop partway through because the control they are about to press has been scrolled off the visible part of the panel, so the run reports a failure that is about the window being short rather than about anything the app got wrong. Fix them so a full sweep tells the truth.
notes:
Reproduced on 2026-09-12 against the probe built from main at that time, BEFORE and AFTER the steady-name change, with identical failures both times, so the steady names are not the cause.

  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/border-effect-walk.json --no-build
  [30 press] FAILED: the control "Slider" is not where a person could click it: it is off the window, or the dock has scrolled it far enough that the panel edge cuts across the point a press would land on.

  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/glow-effect-walk.json --no-build
  [30 press] FAILED: the control "Color" is not where a person could click it: ...

  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/label-fills-a-row-walk.json --no-build
  [23 press] FAILED: the control "Fixed" is not where a person could click it: ...

The baseline was taken by running the walk files as they stand at git HEAD (git show HEAD:Scripts/playtest/<name>.json > /tmp/...) and they failed at the same step numbers with the same messages.

The `reveal` step exists for exactly this (docs/design/playtest-harness.md) and landed on 2026-09-08; these three were never given one. Three earlier tasks about scrolled-away controls are all marked done: an-alignment-button-the-panel-has-scrolled-away, a-switch-in-the-parts-list-the-walk-cannot-reach, a-control-scrolled-out-of-its-own-section-gets-c. So this is most likely three walks that were missed rather than a new defect, but worth checking whether the window these three ask for is simply too short for what they open.
acceptance: Scripts/playtest.sh runs border-effect-walk.json, glow-effect-walk.json and label-fills-a-row-walk.json to completion
Each one still proves what its seed says it proves, rather than having the failing claim deleted
No new walk in the set fails as a result
